final_message:
Reproduced at 4f08332 (ESLint 9.14.0, `@eslint/config-array` 0.18.0). The bug is still there at this revision.

I'm on Linux, so the script fakes Windows. Before loading ESLint it sets `process.platform` to `"win32"`, makes every `require("path")` / `require("node:path")` return `path.win32`, and sets the cwd to `C:\Project`. It then compares `F:\foo.js` (another drive) with `C:\Other\foo.js` (same drive, outside the cwd).

Run it with `node repro/windows-cross-drive.js`. It exits with code 1 when the bug shows up:

| | `C:\Other\foo.js` | `F:\foo.js` |
|---|---|---|
| `path.win32.relative(cwd, file)` | `..\Other\foo.js` | `F:\foo.js` (absolute, no `..`) |
| `Linter#verify` | "No matching configuration found" (ignored) | `no-undef: 'foo' is not defined` (linted) |
| `ESLint` with `overrideConfigFile: true` (= `--no-config-lookup`): `isPathIgnored` | true | **false** |
| same `ESLint`: `lintText` | "File ignored because outside of base path" | `no-undef` error (linted) |

**Likely cause:** `@eslint/config-array` decides whether a file is outside the base path with `path.relative(basePath, filePath).startsWith("..")`. That check is in `getConfigWithStatus`, `shouldIgnorePath` and `isDirectoryIgnored` in `node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs`. On Windows, `path.relative` across drives returns the absolute target path, which doesn't start with `..`. So the file is treated as inside the base path, and the default `**/*.js` pattern matches it.

ESLint's own `lib/eslint/eslint-helpers.js` has the same `path.isAbsolute(pattern) ? path.relative(basePath, pattern)` pattern (around lines 165 and 244), so it may be affected too. I haven't checked that path.

**Not covered:** I didn't drive the real CLI with `lintFiles` on `F:\foo.js`, because that reads the actual filesystem and needs a real Windows drive. `lintText` goes through the same config lookup the CLI uses for ignore decisions. If you want it confirmed on real Windows, I can run it on a Windows machine.

The patch only adds `repro/windows-cross-drive.js`; no ESLint source is changed.
